question: Japan dislocations — principal's premise: 'Japan is down on currency reasons, not fundamentals'
PREMISE_INVERTED: the yen did not weaken, it SURGED. USD/JPY 163.85 (Jul-23) -> 157.19 (Aug-2) = 4.2% yen appreciation, 3.9% of it in three sessions (Jul-29 -> Aug-2). Verified from IBKR IDEALPRO daily mid.

why_that_flips_the_logic.for_a_USD_holder: a yen surge is a TAILWIND, not a translation loss - every yen of Japanese asset is worth ~4% more in dollars. Our sleeve's USD marks were CUSHIONED by it, not caused by it.
why_that_flips_the_logic.for_the_businesses: a yen surge is a genuine FUNDAMENTAL hit to EXPORTERS (yen-denominated earnings fall) - so Japanese equities fell for a real reason, not an artifact. The 'currency not fundamentals' framing is backwards for the export cohort.
why_that_flips_the_logic.where_the_real_dislocation_is: DOMESTIC and IMPORTER businesses. They sell in yen and buy in dollars, so a yen surge is a direct gross-margin TAILWIND - yet they sell off in index sympathy. That is the genuine mispricing this move creates.

3388.T.read: REAL yen-terms decline; FX cushioned it to ~-4.5% USD. The only genuine loser - needs a cause-check, not an FX excuse. My earlier 'FX noise' characterisation of the JP sleeve was WRONG for this name.

6229.T.read: flat in yen; FX is the whole story - USD-positive

screen_output_yen_surge_beneficiaries.name: Yamaya
screen_output_yen_surge_beneficiaries.case: MOST DIRECT: retails IMPORTED alcohol and food in Japan - cost of goods is literally imported, revenue is domestic yen. A 4% yen surge is a straight gross-margin tailwind. Already in the intake at 0.60x book, cleanest PFIC profile on the shelf. Gate noted in the intake: family+AEON lock ~68% so it is a consolidation-or-nothing case.

screen_output_yen_surge_beneficiaries.name: Naigai Tec
screen_output_yen_surge_beneficiaries.case: imports pneumatic/vacuum equipment, sells domestically - same mechanism. But intake flagged +47.5% YTD and guidance pairing +24.5% revenue with only +5.1% profit; courted for a re-entry level, not this price.

screen_output_yen_surge_beneficiaries.name: RIKEI
screen_output_yen_surge_beneficiaries.case: domestic IT integrator reselling imported IBM/HPE hardware - yen strength cuts COGS. Offset: intake flagged FY3/27 operating profit guided -40%, so the fall is a downgrade being priced. The FX tailwind is a mitigant, not a thesis.

screen_output_yen_surge_beneficiaries.name: Cleanup
screen_output_yen_surge_beneficiaries.case: pure-domestic system kitchens; imported steel/resin/appliance inputs get cheaper. Already ranked #2 in the intake on its own merits (strict-denominator sub-book, executed cancel-buyback, +20% guide). The yen surge ADDS a margin tailwind the shelf score cannot see.

cohort_to_AVOID_on_this_move: 7927 Muto Seiko (Vietnam cost base shrinks too)
IMPORTANT_TIMING_CONFLICT: the whole intake prints Q1 this week (two on the intake date, four on Aug 6-7) and five of ten guide FY3/27 profit DOWN. Any yen-surge thesis must survive the print - and the print will be reported at PRE-surge exchange rates, so the FX effect shows up in NEXT quarter's guidance, not this one. Nowcast-before-prints rule applies: court after, not before.
action: court 7955 (Cleanup) and 9994 (Yamaya) as the yen-surge-beneficiary pair AFTER their prints; both are already in the deployment intake so this adds a reason, not a new name. Re-check the FX level at court time - a 4% move in three sessions can retrace as fast.
